tasks.short: Build the yearly HR personnel budget in Excel from AFAS data and CAO tables, then track it monthly.

steps.what: Export positions, salaries and contract hours from AFAS into the budget workbook
Apply CAO wage steps, indexation, pension, social charges and agency rates
Choose hiring, flex mix, training and wage-round assumptions per site
Agree the personnel budget with Finance Director and controller
Compare monthly actuals to budget and explain variances

tasks.design: Replace the budget workbook with a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform that reads AFAS positions and payroll, the agency invoices and a versioned CAO rate table, and writes a cost baseline plus editable scenario parameters. A Power BI page shows scenarios side by side and the monthly actual-versus-budget variance per site and cost type, refreshed with the nightly AFAS extract.
tasks.previous_blocker: CAO rules, agency rates and AFAS exports lived in separate files, and building a reliable rate engine cost more than one yearly Excel exercise.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small, tested rate engine and data job cheap to build, and the nightly AFAS extract for Power BI already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the CAO rate table correct after each wage round, and flex costs that swing with seasonal volume.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing where to spend scarce money (wages, flex, training) and defending that choice with Finance and the works council.

ambition.what: Re-forecast the personnel budget monthly per site instead of once a year, including the cost of each CAO offer during the 2027 round.

tasks.altitude: Less time in Excel, more time on trade-offs; the director owns the scenario assumptions that Finance accepts as input.

reach.task: Workforce cost lines in the company forecast
reach.learn: Use the same rate table and baseline so HR and Finance stop reconciling two numbers.
Keep the rate table as versioned, tested data rather than formulas in a workbook.

evidence.claim: Budgets suit deterministic software built from AFAS positions and CAO tables.
The transport CAO ends 31 Dec 2026, so a 2027 wage round must be costed now.

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract includes positions, contract hours and wage components.
Agency invoices can be exported from the three portals in a fixed format.
unknowns: Whether Finance already keeps a separate personnel cost model in AFAS or Excel.
How the own warehouse CAO wage table is stored and who maintains it.
research_questions: Does the AFAS extract give enough wage component detail to reproduce last year's payroll cost within 1%?
Can all three agency portals export hours and invoices on a schedule?
Will the controller accept the platform baseline as the single source for personnel cost?

tasks.short: Read new labour law, court rulings and CAO news and judge what they mean for Noordhaven.

steps.what: Scan newsletters, government sites, union and court sources for changes
Read items, filter relevance and summarise the point

loop.input: Source item text plus a short profile of Noordhaven (CAOs, sites, flex use, policies)
loop.output: Relevance label, two-line summary with quoted passage and link, and affected policy
loop.check: Every claim must quote the source; links are checked to resolve; items without a quote are dropped
loop.stop: One pass per item, token cap per item; on failure the item goes to the digest as 'unread'
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevance depends on free legal text; keyword filters flood or miss items.

steps.what: Assess impact on CAO talks, policies, costs and legal risk
Brief management team, HRBPs and works council on changes

loop.input: Approved impact notes of the month
loop.output: Two-page brief in Dutch, one section per audience
loop.check: Director edits and approves; brief only cites approved notes
loop.stop: One draft per month; if rejected, director writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot turn varied notes into readable prose per audience.

tasks.design: A scheduled job fetches fixed sources (rechtspraak.nl, overheid.nl, Staatscourant, FNV, CNV, employer association pages) into a SharePoint list, and a bounded model step labels relevance and writes cited summaries for a weekly digest in Teams. The director writes the impact notes; a second bounded step drafts the monthly brief from them, marked as AI-generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal text is unstructured and Dutch, and summarisers made up points without sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Current models summarise Dutch legal text with quoted citations well enough for a reviewed digest, at low cost.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what a ruling means for Noordhaven's own CAO and staff, and sources behind paywalls.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change matters for the people and the bargaining position, and taking responsibility for advice.

ambition.what: A monthly plain-language legal and CAO brief for the 30 site and shift managers, who get nothing today.

tasks.altitude: Reading time drops; the director spends it on impact judgement and on the 2027 CAO round preparation.

reach.learn: Use the cited digest to update policy answers and flag outdated SharePoint policies.

reach.task: Applying wage and tax rule changes
reach.learn: Receive tagged items that touch payroll in time for month close.

evidence.claim: Legislation and CAO study suits model summaries with citations at autonomy 3.
Generated content must be disclosed under AI Act Art. 50.
FNV asks for worker say over AI at the CAO table, so union news needs close tracking.

assumptions: The sources the director reads today are mostly public or reachable by subscription feed.
Content is public, so no personal data enters the model.
unknowns: Which paid legal sources Noordhaven subscribes to and their terms on automated reading.
Whether the employer association shares CAO bargaining news in a feed.
research_questions: Over one month, does the digest catch every item the director flagged by hand?
How many summaries have a citation that does not support the claim?
Do site managers read a monthly brief if offered?

tasks.short: Run job evaluation: describe jobs, score them in the function system, set the scale, handle objections.

steps.what: Collect evaluation request and current job description from manager
Rewrite description in standard format and find comparable reference jobs

loop.input: Manager's job description and the function house reference jobs
loop.output: Description in the standard template and three nearest reference jobs with differences listed
loop.check: C&B specialist checks against interview with the manager; no score is produced
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; else manual
loop.why_not_simpler: Job descriptions are free text in varying shapes; matching on titles fails.

steps.what: Score the job and place it in a salary scale in committee
Check cost and equal-pay effects for current job holders
Record grade in AFAS, inform employees, handle objections

tasks.design: Configure an AFAS workflow for evaluation requests with the description attached, and add a bounded model step that rewrites descriptions into the template and lists nearest reference jobs, without scoring. A Power BI page shows the cost and pay-gap effect of a proposed grade; the committee scores, and AFAS generates the letter after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Descriptions arrived as free text in mail, and matching them to the function house needed an expert reading each one.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now rewrite and compare job texts reliably, and the AFAS workflow and Power BI extract already exist.
tasks.still_hard: Scoring remains judgement, objections are personal, and the works council must trust that the method is neutral.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing a job's real content fairly and explaining a grade face to face when someone objects.

ambition.what: An equal-pay check per job family, refreshed yearly, ready for the EU pay transparency rules.

tasks.altitude: The director chairs fewer, better prepared committees and owns the reference job set.

reach.learn: Maintain reference jobs as structured data the drafting step can use.
Start from the standard job description so vacancy and grade match.

evidence.claim: Job evaluation fits a copilot at autonomy 2; rate jobs, not people.
A ranking tool on people is high-risk from 2 Dec 2027 even with a final human click; tools without a score on people can fall outside.
A works council can have advice or consent rights over an AI decision.

assumptions: Noordhaven uses a function system (CAO grid or a method such as ORBA) with reference jobs on file.
The drafting step never scores jobs or people.
unknowns: Which job evaluation method each CAO prescribes and who holds its licence.
Whether the works council sees this change as needing consent under Art. 27 WOR.
research_questions: Do C&B reviewers accept at least 80% of drafted descriptions with small edits?
Does the function method licence allow using its reference texts in a model prompt?
Does the works council agree that a no-score drafting step is outside high-risk use?

tasks.short: Forecast staffing needs per site and shift from volume plans, turnover and absence.

steps.what: Gather headcount, turnover, absence and flex hours per site
Collect volume and client forecasts from operations and site managers
Model demand per site and shift, attrition, retirements and absence
Choose scenarios: hire, flex, overtime or training per site
Present the plan to management and Finance

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform builds the workforce baseline from AFAS and the agency portals, and a small form (Microsoft Forms or a SharePoint list) collects site volume plans in a fixed format. A deterministic model with stated assumptions turns them into FTE need per site and shift under three scenarios in Power BI, feeding the budget and the recruiters' pipeline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volume plans came in different shapes by mail, and agency hours were not joined to AFAS data.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract and cheap AI-assisted coding make the joins and a transparent scenario model a few days of work.
tasks.still_hard: Client volume is uncertain and seasonal; forecast quality only shows months later.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding how much risk to carry between fixed staff and flex, and getting site managers to commit to their numbers.

ambition.what: Quarterly rolling forecast per site and shift, instead of one yearly plan, timed before the seasonal flex peak.

tasks.altitude: The director moves from compiling numbers to setting the fixed-versus-flex policy per site with operations.

reach.learn: Open requisitions from the approved plan before the peak, not after.
Share one set of volume drivers between HR and Finance.

evidence.claim: Workday Work Intelligence (beta) cut a planned 50 hires to 42 in a demo by planning from tasks.
Personnel forecasts should show scenarios, not one number, on the analyst's metric layer.

assumptions: Operations has a volume forecast per site, even if rough.
Aggregated forecasts use no personal data beyond what Power BI already holds.
unknowns: Who in operations owns volume forecasts and how often they change.
Whether agency hours can be tied to sites and shifts.
research_questions: Would last year's model have predicted the actual flex peak within 15%?
Will site managers fill a fixed-format volume form each quarter?
Can agency portal data be joined to AFAS cost centres without manual mapping?

role.altitude: From compiling budgets, forecasts and legal reading by hand to designing the HR operating system: which steps run alone, which need review, and what the works council has agreed to.
reach: Finance Director: shared personnel cost baseline and volume drivers
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: owns the data jobs and Power BI layer these tasks use
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: CAO rate table and function house as structured data
HR Business Partners: cited legal digest feeding policy advice
skills_to_grow: Setting autonomy levels and approval gates per automated step
AI Act and WOR compliance for HR tools (Art. 50 disclosure, high-risk from Dec 2027, Art. 24/27 consultation)
Scenario thinking for workforce cost and flex risk
Costing union demands, including the FNV ask for say over AI
role.ambitious_version: One governed HR data platform where budget, forecast and grading run from the same AFAS and agency data, re-forecast monthly per site, with an AI agreement signed with the works council and taken into the 2027 CAO round.
